description: Statements of the curator v5 exhibition in live_run_2026-10-14.json, annotated by reading the cited sources (all are headlines or one-line records). A fact-checker 'flags' a statement when one of its unsupported_claims for that section contains any of the 'match' strings (case-insensitive). 'should_flag' is our judgement of whether the statement adds something the sources do not say.

statements.text: extreme heat waves triggered visible protests in both Libya and Tunisia
statements.why: Source: 'Protests in Libya, Tunisia Amid Extreme Heat Wave'. 'Amid' reports co-occurrence, not causation.

statements.text: rising temperatures directly precipitated public grievance, linking environmental vulnerability to the breakdown of social order
statements.why: Same headline; no source reports a breakdown of social order or a direct causal link.
The sources are from 2026; the revolution was in 2011, fifteen years earlier. No source gives 'eleven years'.

statements.text: la décentralisation administrative n'a pas suffi à prévenir l'effondrement de l'infrastructure
statements.why: The cited headline only reports a serious electricity crisis five years after Saïed's exceptional measures; decentralisation is not mentioned.

statements.text: In 2026, Tunisia's economy grew by only 2.1%
statements.why: Supported: headline 'Tunisia Economy Grows 2.1% as Debt Crowds Out Firms', dated 2026.
The source only names FTDES; it does not describe it. (FTDES is the Tunisian Forum for Economic and Social Rights, an NGO, not a trade union.)

statements.text: leading to a 'civilizational fatigue' among the populace
domestic labor market realities, where structural deficits and long-term unemployment persisted
statements.why: Factual sentence with no citation; the section's only source is the internet-usage figure.

statements.text: By 2024, internet penetration in Tunisia reached 76.5%
statements.why: Supported: World Bank record 'Individuals using the Internet (% of population) for Tunisia in 2024: 76.5'.

statements.text: In Sydney, street art explicitly themed on climate change
statements.why: Supported: 'Street art in Sydney. Climate change. 2026'.
